title: az boards query --project ${project} --wiql "SELECT [System.Id], [System.Title], [System.AssignedTo], [System.Tags], [System.CreatedDate], [System.IterationPath] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = @project AND [System.State] NOT IN ('Closed', 'Done', 'Removed') AND [System.Id] > ${after} ORDER BY [System.Id] ASC" --output json
description: One page of the project's open work items, whose number, title, assignee, tags, creation, and iteration `modules/bash/forge/ado.sh` (forge/ado:open-issues) and `modules/bash/tracker/ado.sh` (tracker/ado:open-issues) read and `modules/jq/forge.jq` folds with ado_issues, ado_assignees, and ado_tags; every call kit makes through forge/ado:az also carries --org ${organization} --detect false --only-show-errors. The extension runs the query, https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/azure/devops/wit/wiql/query-by-wiql?view=azure-devops-rest-7.1, then reads the first 1000 work items it finds with only the columns it selects, https://learn.microsoft.com/rest/api/azure/devops/wit/work-items/list?view=azure-devops-rest-7.1, each a WorkItem as boards-work-item-show.schema.json gives one, and prints nothing at all when the query finds none, which kit reads as []. It says nothing of the work items past the first 1000, so kit asks for those whose id is above ${after}, 0 at first, in the order of their ids, and reads an answer of 1000 as a full page: it asks again with the highest id it read, until a page holds fewer. That the extension stops at 1000 was not seen against a live organization.

System.State.description: The process template's state: Closed, Done, and Removed are closed, any other open.

System.AssignedTo.description: An IdentityRef, left out when nobody is assigned; uniqueName is the login az signs in as.

System.Tags.description: The tags, one text joined by "; ", left out when there are none.

System.IterationPath.description: The iteration's path, the project's name first: empowerite\Sprint 4.
